newsitem.title: USA: Americans trust Clinton more than Gingrich - poll.
newsitem.headline: Americans trust Clinton more than Gingrich - poll.

text.p: Americans by a wide margin think President Clinton is more honest and trustworthy than House Speaker Newt Gingrich, a poll released Friday said.

With the Republican House leader's ethics violations under a spotlight, the Harris Poll said the Democratic president was viewed as more honest and trustworthy by 57 percent to Gingrich's 22 percent, even though Clinton has faced charges of unethical behaviour.
Even among Republicans, 47 percent thought Gingrich was more honest, 26 percent said Clinton was and 20 percent said there was no difference between the two. Six percent did not know.

Among Democrats, 79 percent of Democrats felt Clinton was The poll was released as the House ethics committee was preparing to hold a public hearing Friday on punishment for Gingrich's admitted ethics violations.

"This poll appears to confirm the judgment of political commentators, who have argued that keeping Newt Gingrich as House Speaker will make it harder for the Republicans to damage Clinton with charges of unethical and illegal behaviour related to Democratic fundraising, Paula Jones, Whitewater and other scandals," said Humphrey Taylor, chairman and CEO of Louis Harris and Associates, which conducted the poll.
The telephone poll of 1,005 adults in the United States between Jan. 9 and 13 had a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.

Gingrich admitted Dec. 21 he had failed to get legal advice to ensure compliance with a ban on using tax-exempt funds for partisan political activity and had given false information to investigators. He was narrowly re-elected House Speaker Jan. 7, with nine Republicans refusing to vote for him because of his admitted ethics violations.

Clinton's own troubles have included the Democratic Party returning hundreds of thousands of dollars in illegal campaign contributions and a long-running special prosecutor's investigation into the so-called Whitewater affair, an Arkansas land deal that went bad for Clinton and his wife Hillary Rodham Clinton.

In addition, a former Arkansas state worker, Paula Jones, took her charges of sexual harassment against Clinton to the Supreme Court this week, seeking to have the case heard by a lower court while Clinton is still in office.
